t: Born in a Guaraní mission town and educated in Spain, San Martín served the Spanish crown for more than twenty years, fought in the Peninsular War and then returned to South America to serve the independence movement in Buenos Aires in 1812.

As governor of Cuyo he raised the Army of the Andes, led it across the mountains in about a month and won at Chacabuco and Maipú, the battle that secured Chilean independence, before sailing to Peru and declaring its independence on 28 July 1821.

After a closed-door meeting with Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil in July 1822, whose content historians can only infer, he resigned as Protector of Peru, left politics and the army, and spent the rest of his life in Europe.
dyk: Crossing the Andes was not the first military expedition to cross the range; what set San Martín's apart was the size of his army and that it had to be ready for combat right after the crossing.
ev: San Martín is born in Yapeyú, in the Guaraní missions; his father was the local governor
He reaches Buenos Aires on 9 March and begins to raise the Regiment of Mounted Grenadiers
He takes office as governor of Cuyo on 6 September and begins organising the Army of the Andes
The Army of the Andes wins at Chacabuco on 12 February and enters Santiago the next day
The patriots defeat the royalist army at Maipú, which secures Chilean independence
After taking Lima, he declares the independence of Peru on 28 July and becomes Protector
He meets Simón Bolívar at Guayaquil on 26 July and soon resigns as Protector of Peru
He dies at Boulogne-sur-Mer in France

f.born: 25 February 1778 (the year is disputed; most documents point to 1777 or 1778) in Yapeyú, Corrientes, an Indian reduction of the Guaraní people; son of the Spanish officer Juan de San Martín and Gregoria Matorras del Ser
f.died: 17 August 1850 at three o'clock, in his house at Boulogne-sur-Mer, France, almost blind and in poor health, shortly after news of the Argentine victory against the Anglo-French blockade
f.role: Spanish army officer; colonel and commander of the Regiment of Mounted Grenadiers; commander of the Army of the North (1814); governor of Cuyo from 6 September 1814; leader of the Army of the Andes; Protector of Peru from 1821 to 1822
f.known: the Regiment of Mounted Grenadiers and the battle of San Lorenzo; organising the Army of the Andes in Cuyo; the Crossing of the Andes; the victories of Chacabuco and Maipú in Chile; the naval expedition to Peru and the declaration of its independence in 1821; the Guayaquil meeting with Simón Bolívar
